questions.question: A certain quantity of a 35% sugar solution is mixed with 8 litres of a 48% sugar solution to obtain a 40% sugar solution. How many litres of the 35% sugar solution was there in the mixture?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the alligation cross method, the ratio of quantities = (48 − 40) : (40 − 35) = 8 : 5

Here, 5 parts correspond to 8 litres of the 48% solution.

So, 1 part = 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 litres.

Quantity of 35% solution = 8 parts = 8 × 1.6 = 12.8 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.8 litres.**

questions.question: The area of a trapezium is 140 cm² and the perpendicular distance between its parallel sides is 7 cm. If the length of one of the parallel sides is 28 cm, what is the length of the other parallel side?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of parallel sides = (2 × Area) ÷ Height

⇒ Sum = (2 × 140) ÷ 7 = 280 ÷ 7 = 40 cm

Other parallel side = Sum − Given side

⇒ Other side = 40 − 28 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of trapezium = 140 cm²

Perpendicular distance (h) = 7 cm

One parallel side (a) = 28 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = (1/2) × (a + b) × h

Where 'a' and 'b' are the lengths of the parallel sides and 'h' is the height.

 

 
• 
 h = 7 cm
 a = 28 cm
 b = ?
 Area = 140 cm²

**Calculation:**

⇒ 140 = (1/2) × (28 + b) × 7

⇒ 140 × 2 = (28 + b) × 7

⇒ 280 = (28 + b) × 7

⇒ 280 ÷ 7 = 28 + b

⇒ 40 = 28 + b

⇒ b = 40 − 28

⇒ b = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Trapezium

The perimeter is the sum of all its four sides. Perimeter = a + b + c + d, where a and b are parallel sides and c and d are non-parallel sides.

Median of a Trapezium

The median (or mid-segment) connects the midpoints of the non-parallel sides. Its length is the average of the parallel sides: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Isosceles Trapezium

In an isosceles trapezium, the non-parallel sides are equal in length, and the base angles are equal. The diagonals of an isosceles trapezium are also equal.</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 7,500 amounts to Rs. 11,700 in 8 years at a certain rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total **Simple Interest (SI)** earned in 8 years = 11,700 − 7,500 = ₹4,200.

**SI** for 1 year = 4,200 ÷ 8 = ₹525.

**Rate of interest (R%)** = (Yearly Interest ÷ Principal) × 100.

**R%** = (525 ÷ 7,500) × 100 = 525 ÷ 75 = 7%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹7,500

**Amount (A)** = ₹11,700

**Time (T)** = 8 years

**Formula Used:**

1) **Simple Interest (SI)** = **Amount (A)** − **Principal (P)**

2) **Rate (R)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c7afde24a74f6e5423cf016fa79194add71486e21ea38d3670c5a3d90064fd4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **SI** = 11,700 − 7,500 = 4,200

⇒ **R** = (4,200 × 100) ÷ (7,500 × 8)

⇒ **R** = 420,000 ÷ 60,000

⇒ **R** = 7%

**∴ The correct answer is 7%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is **Principal**, R is **Rate per annum**, and T is **Time in years**.

Total Amount Formula

A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Rate and Time Relation

For a constant **Principal**, the **Simple Interest** is directly proportional to both **Rate** and **Time**.

SI vs CI

In **Simple Interest**, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal, whereas in **Compound Interest**, interest is calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest.

questions.question: A can do a job alone in 66 days. B can do it alone in 55 days, while A, B and C working together can complete the job in 22 days. In how many days can C do the job alone?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(66, 55, 22) = 330 units.

Efficiency of **A** = 5, **B** = 6, and (**A+B+C**) = 15.

Efficiency of **C** = 15 − (5 + 6) = 4.

Time taken by **C** = 330 ÷ 4 = 82.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 82.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 330 ÷ 66 = 5 units/day.

questions.question: If 15% of A ∶ 25% of B :: 8 ∶ 11, then A ∶ B is equal to:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **proportion** a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means.

(15% × A) × 11 = (25% × B) × 8

15 × A × 11 = 25 × B × 8 (Percentage cancels out)

A / B = (25 × 8) / (15 × 11) = (5 × 8) / (3 × 11) = 40 / 33

**∴ The correct answer is 40 : 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**15% of A : 25% of B = 8 : 11**

Ratio of **x% of A** to **y% of B** is (x × A) / (y × B).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ddc52cb9d75400c212c3014c1c9dc24c6d303a000cba66348921e9f06eca6ebc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (15/100) × A / (25/100) × B = 8 / 11

⇒ (15 × A) / (25 × B) = 8 / 11

⇒ (3 × A) / (5 × B) = 8 / 11

⇒ 3A × 11 = 8 × 5B

⇒ 33A = 40B

⇒ A / B = 40 / 33

**∴ The correct answer is 40 : 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Proportion

If a : b :: c : d, then the product of extremes (a × d) is always equal to the product of means (b × c).

Percentage Ratios

When comparing percentages of two different quantities, the common denominator (100) can be canceled out directly: x% of A / y% of B = (x × A) / (y × B).

Compounded Ratio

The compounded ratio of (a : b) and (c : d) is (a × c) : (b × d). This is useful when multiple ratios are linked.</p

A question is given, followed by three statements labelled I, II and III. Identify which of the statements is/are sufficient to answer the question.

**Question**:

What is Mala's age?

**Statements**:

I. The sum of Rohan's, Sheela's and Mala's age is 95.

II. Rohan is younger than Mala.

III. Mala is 10 years older than Sheela.

options.text: Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement III alone is not sufficient

Statement I, II and III together are not sufficient.

questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let the age of Rohan, Sheela, and Mala be R, SH, and M respectively.

According to the statement II,

M > R ....(1)

According to the statement III,

M = SH + 10

⇒ SH = M - 10 ....(2)

According to the statement I,

R + SH + M = 95 ....(3)

⇒ R + M - 10 + M = 95

⇒ R + 2M = 95 + 10

⇒ R + 2M = 105 ....(4)

Even using (1), (2), (3), and (4) simultaneously, we can not evaluate M.

**∴ Statement I, II, and III together are not sufficient.**

questions.question: Four years ago, the age of the mother was 13 times the age of her daughter. Two years hence, the mother's age will be 4 times the daughter's age. After how many years will the mother's age be 3 times that of her daughter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of Mother to Daughter (4 yrs ago) = 13 : 1 (Diff = 12)

**Ratio** (2 yrs hence) = 4 : 1 (Diff = 3 × 4 = 12) → 16 : 4

Change in units = 16 − 13 = 3 units; Total time gap = 4 + 2 = 6 years.

∴ 3 units = 6 years ⇒ 1 unit = 2 years. Mother's current age = (16 × 2) − 2 = 30; Daughter = (4 × 2) − 2 = 6.

Let after **x years** ratio be 3 : 1 ⇒ (30 + x) = 3(6 + x) ⇒ 30 + x = 18 + 3x ⇒ 2x = 12 ⇒ x = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Mother's age was 13 times daughter's 4 years ago. After 2 years, it will be 4 times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/872172a9f55a41c5dc625896db01f4108edde1d9bc7c06fb31694810ad49856d.png] 

Let the age of the **daughter** and **mother** 4 years ago be x and 13x respectively.

Current age: Mother = 13x + 4, Daughter = x + 4

Two years hence: Mother = 13x + 6, Daughter = x + 6

⇒ 13x + 6 = 4(x + 6)

⇒ 13x + 6 = 4x + 24

⇒ 9x = 18 ⇒ x = 2

⇒ **Current Mother's age** = 13(2) + 4 = 30 years

⇒ **Current Daughter's age** = 2 + 4 = 6 years

Let after **'n' years**, mother's age be 3 times daughter's age:

⇒ 30 + n = 3(6 + n)

⇒ 30 + n = 18 + 3n

⇒ 2n = 12 ⇒ n = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Balancing Method

To solve age problems quickly, balance the **difference in ratio parts** by multiplying the ratios by the difference of the opposite ratio's parts.

General Formula

If current ages are M and D, then after 'n' years, the ratio becomes (M + n) / (D + n) = R₁ / R₂.</p

questions.question:
The difference between the external and internal curved surface areas of a 7 cm long cylindrical metallic pipe is 110 cm² . If the pipe is made of 302.5 cm³ metal, then find the inner radius of the pipe.

(Use π = (22)/(7) )
questions.solution:
Given:

The difference between the external and internal curved surface areas of a 7 cm long cylindrical metallic pipe is 110 cm2 .

The pipe is made of 302.5 cm3 metal

Concept used:

In the case of a cylindrical pipe, volume = π × (R²₁ - R²₂) × H

Here R₁ and R₂ are the external and internal radius of the pipe and H = Height of the pipe

Curved surface area of a cylinder = 2πRH

Here R = Radius of the base and H = Height

A2 - B2 = (A + B) (A - B)

Calculation:

Let the outer and inner radius of the pipe be R and r centimeter respectively.

According to the question,

2πR × 7 - 2πr × 7 = 110

⇒ 2 × (22)/(7) × 7 × (R - r) = 110

⇒ 44(R - r) = 110

⇒ (R - r) = 110/44

⇒ (R - r) = 2.5 ....(1)

According to the question,

π × (R² - r²) × 7 = 302.5

⇒ (22)/(7) × 7 × (R² - r²) = 302.5

⇒ (R2 - r2) = 302.5/22

⇒ (R2 - r2) = 13.75

⇒ (R + r) (R - r) = 13.75

⇒ (R + r) × 2.5 = 13.75 (From 1)

⇒ (R + r) = 13.75/2.5

⇒ (R + r) = 5.5 ....(2)

Solving (1) and (2),

R = 4 and r = 1.5

∴ The inner radius of the pipe is 1.5 cm.

questions.question: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular octagon?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **regular polygon** with **n** sides, each interior angle is calculated as:

Each Interior Angle = ((n − 2) × 180°) ÷ n

For a **regular octagon**, n = 8.

Each Interior Angle = ((8 − 2) × 180°) ÷ 8 = (6 × 180°) ÷ 8 = 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Polygon type = **Regular Octagon**

Number of sides (n) = **8**

**Formula Used:**

1. **Exterior Angle** of a regular polygon = 360° ÷ n

2. **Interior Angle** + **Exterior Angle** = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9329e9525342190d51209b0bdf52c07c5c1cc8f2b28ed298c909a8ff7e0806a8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Each **Exterior Angle** = 360° ÷ 8

⇒ Each **Exterior Angle** = 45°

⇒ Each **Interior Angle** = 180° − 45°

⇒ Each **Interior Angle** = 135°

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of any n-sided polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For an **octagon**, it is 1080°.

Number of Diagonals

The number of **diagonals** in a polygon with n sides is n(n − 3) ÷ 2. For an **octagon**, it is 8(8 − 3) ÷ 2 = 20.

External Angle Property

The **sum of all exterior angles** of any convex polygon is always 360°, regardless of the number of sides.</p

questions.question: A batsman scored 84 runs in his 12th innings, thereby improving his average score per innings by 4 runs. What is the average score per innings of the batsman after the 12th innings?
questions.solution:
Given:

The batsman scored 84 runs in his 12th innings, thereby improving his average score per innings by 4 runs.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Let the average of the batman in the first 11 innings be N.

The total run scored by the batsman in the first 11 innings = 11 × N = 11N

The total run scored by the batsman in all 12 innings = 11N + 84

New average score after 12th innings = N + 4

According to the question,

(11N + 84)/12 = (N + 4)

⇒ (11N + 84) = (N + 4) × 12

⇒ 11N + 84 = 12N + 48

⇒ 12N - 11N = 84 - 48

⇒ N = 36

Now, N + 4 = 36 + 4

⇒ 40

**∴ 40 is the average score per innings of the batsman after the 12th innings.**

questions.question: Aamish's birthday on 25th February 2020 was a Tuesday. Which day of the week was his brother's birthday, which was on 13th May 2020?
questions.solution:
We know that: 

In an ordinary year, there are 365 days and on dividing 365 by 7,

 
• We get remainder = 1 so this extra one day is taken as odd day.

Similarly, in an leap year, there are 366 days and on dividing 366 by 7,

 
• we get remainder = 2 so this extra two days is taken as odd days.

Thus, the remainder, which we get after dividing the number of days by 7 is considered as odd days.

Given Aamish's birthday on 25th February 2020 was a Tuesday.

As 2020 is a leap year number of days in month of February = 29 days

 
• Remaining days in February after 25th = 4 days.
 
• Number of days in month of March = 31 days.
 
• Number of days in month of April = 30 days.
 
• Number of days in month of May by 13th May 2020 = 13 days

Number of days from 25th February 2020 to 13th May 2020 = 4 + 31 + 30 + 13.

Number of days from 25th February 2020 to 13th May 2020 = 78

**The number of odd days from 25th February 2020 to 13th May 2020 = 1 odd day.**

∴ On 25th February 2020, **it was a Tuesday + 1 = Wednesday**

∴ Here, Aamish's brother's birthday, which was on 13th May 2020 is 'Wednesday'.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Wednesday".**

questions.question: Manyata rowed a certain distance downstream in 2 hours while it took her 30 minutes more to row the same distance upstream. How much time will she take to make the two-way journey in still water?
questions.solution:
Given:

Manyata rowed a certain distance downstream in 2 hours while it took her 30 minutes more i.e. 2.5 hours to row the same distance upstream.

Concept used:

Time × Speed = Distance

While rowing upstream, the upstream speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

While rowing downstream, the downstream speed is the addition of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

30 minutes = 0.5 hour

Calculation:

Let S be the speed of the boat in the still water and R be the speed of the water.

Now,

The downstream speed = (S + R)

The upstream speed = (S - R)

According to the question,

(S + R) × 2 = (S - R) × 2.5

⇒ (S + R)/(S - R) = 2.5/2

⇒ 2S + 2R = 2.5S - 2.5R

⇒ 0.5S = 4.5R

⇒ S/R = 4.5/0.5

⇒ S/R = 9/1

Let the common ratio be Q.

The speed of the boat in still water is 9Q and the speed of the water Q.

Rowing distance = (S + R) × 2

⇒ (9Q + Q) × 2

⇒ 20Q

Time taken to complete the two-way journey in still water

⇒ (20Q × 2)/9Q

⇒ 4{4 over 9} hours

⇒ 4 hours ({4 over 9} × 60) minutes

⇒ 4 hours 26 minutes {2 over 3} seconds

⇒ 4 hours 26 minutes ({2 over 3} × 60) seconds

⇒ 4 hours 26 minutes 40 seconds

**∴ She will take 4 hours 26 minutes 40 seconds to make the two-way journey in still water.**

questions.question: Embarked upon in 1965-66 as an integral part of the Green Revolution, the High Yielding Varieties Programme (HYVP) included which of the following crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat, rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The High Yielding Varieties Programme (HYVP),** which was launched in** 1965–1966 as a crucial component** of the so-called** Green Revolution, **was an effort to transform archaic Indian agriculture, particularly with regard to a few crops.
 
• Following the Joint Report on the operation of the HYVP in India, which was published in 1971 by the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) and **the Australian National Academy,** the same team published a more technical and in-depth evaluation of the program's success from 1970 to 1975 in 1976.
 
• The 1976 study, which focused only on wheat and paddy, aimed to clarify the long-term trends in these crops for use in more analytical planning and agricultural research. 
 
• The method used to choose the states, districts, blocks, and villages was the same as the method used in the earlier research.
 
• HYVP area targets of more than one lakh hectares for the Fourth Five Year Plan were granted to the States that grew the chosen crop widely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The set of research and technology transfer initiatives that took place between 1950 and the late 1960s, known as the **"Green Revolution," or the "Third Agricultural Revolution" (after the Neolithic Revolution and the British Agricultural Revolution)**, increased agricultural production in various parts of the world, starting most noticeably in the late 1960s.
 
• As a result of the activities, new technologies were adopted, including high-yielding (HYV) crop varieties, particularly dwarf wheat and rice.
 
• It was connected to mechanised farming, artificial fertilisers, agrochemicals, controlled water supply (typically using irrigation), and innovative farming techniques.
 
• These were all viewed as a** "bundle of activities" **that could replace** "conventional"** technology and be used as a whole.

questions.question: The ratio of the speeds of a bus and a car is 7 ∶ 11. If the car covers a distance of 396 km in 6 hours, what is the speed of the bus in km/h?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Car speed** = 396 ÷ 6 = 66 km/h.

According to the **ratio** 7 : 11, the **car speed** is represented by 11 units.

11 units → 66 km/h ⇒ 1 unit = 6 km/h.

**Bus speed** (7 units) = 7 × 6 = 42 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of speeds (Bus : Car) = 7 : 11

**Distance** covered by car = 396 km

**Time** taken by car = 6 hr

**Formula used:**

**Speed** = **Distance** ÷ **Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07e611de366a709bab7c0ae423e6b269f8a62bbd26752a497a31985d86e75cc8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Speed of Car** = 396 ÷ 6

⇒ **Speed of Car** = 66 km/h

⇒ Let the **Speed of Bus** be 7x and **Speed of Car** be 11x.

⇒ 11x = 66

⇒ x = 66 ÷ 11 = 6

⇒ **Speed of Bus** = 7x = 7 × 6

⇒ **Speed of Bus** = 42 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert speed from **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: The average of five consecutive natural numbers is 12. What will be the average of the seven numbers if the next two natural numbers are also included?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average of five consecutive natural numbers is 12.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Let the first natural number be N.

According to the question,

N + (N + 1) + (N + 2) + (N + 3) + (N + 4) = 12 × 5

⇒ 5N + 10 = 60

⇒ 5N = 50

⇒ N = 50/5

⇒ N = 10

Sum of the seven numbers

⇒ N + (N + 1) + (N + 2) + (N + 3) + (N + 4) + (N + 5) + (N + 6)

⇒ 7N + 21

⇒ 7 × 10 + 21

⇒ 91

Average of the seven numbers = 91/7 = 13

**∴ The average of the seven numbers if the next two natural numbers are also included will be 13.**

questions.question: The Sattriya dance form was introduced in the ______ by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam, Mahapurusha Sankaradeva.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15th century A.D.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The great Assamese reformer and Vaishnava saint Mahapurusha Sankaradeva** established the Sattriya dancing style in the 15th century A.D. as a potent means of spreading the Vaishnava religion.
 
• Later, the dancing style developed and broadened as a distinct dance genre.
 
• The Sattras, which are Vaishnava mathematics or monasteries, have dedicatedly nourished and protected this neo-Vaishnava treasure of Assamese dance and drama for generations.
 
• This dance form has been appropriately dubbed Sattriya due to its religious nature and connection to the Sattras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sankaradeva **invented this dance style by fusing components from many treatises, regional folk dances, and his singular perspective.
 
• Ojapali and Devadasi, two dance styles with numerous classical elements, were popular in Assam before the neo-Vaishnava movement.
 
• The branch of Hinduism known as Vaishnavism regards Lord Vishnu or one of his incarnations as the only true God. Vaishnavites and Vaishnavas are terms for followers of Vaishnavism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Srimanta Sankardev **was an Assamese saint-scholar, poet, writer, dancer, actor, singer, artist, social-religious reformer, and significant person in the cultural and religious history of Assam, India, Srimanta Sankardev lived in the 15th and 16th centuries.
 
• The creation of new genres of music (Borgeet), theatrical performance (Ankia Naat, Bhaona), dance (Sattriya), and literary language (Sattriya) are all credited to him (Brajavali).
 
• Additionally, he left behind a sizable literary corpus that includes poetry, theological writings, and trans-created scriptures (Bhagavat of Sankardev) in Sanskrit, Assamese, and Brajavali.
